glossary: Agent Reach: 项目名；CLI: 命令行工具；MCP: Model Context Protocol 接入方式；OpenCLI: 桌面浏览器登录态后端；doctor: 渠道体检命令；exec 权限: OpenClaw 执行 shell 命令的权限；Cookie: 本地登录凭据；backend: 平台接入后端；zero-config: 无需额外配置；MIT: 开源许可证；v1.5.0: 本次 release 版本。

ambiguities: README says the project is completely free but also mentions a possible server-proxy cost of about $1 per month; edited text treats local use as free and server proxy as a possible cost, without resolving all deployment-cost details.
Project casing varies between Agent-Reach and agent-reach; canonical metadata is preserved in titles while command-style lowercase appears in technical references.

claims.text: Agent Reach is the Panniantong/Agent-Reach repository, a Python project under the MIT License.
Its stated aim is to give an AI agent a single CLI for reading and searching internet platforms.
The README describes Agent Reach as a capability layer that handles backend selection, installation, health checks, and routing, while the agent directly calls upstream tools for actual reading.
It targets users of command-line-capable AI agents such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, Cursor, and Windsurf.
The README says the maintainer offers enterprise Agent customization and implementation cooperation.

Representative supported scenarios include web pages, YouTube subtitles and search, RSS, GitHub, Twitter/X, Bilibili, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, Xiaohongshu, LinkedIn, Boss直聘, V2EX, Xueqiu, and Xiaoyuzhou podcasts.
A default installation can activate several zero-configuration channels, and login-required channels are configured only after the agent asks the user.
Installation and updates can be started by sending the agent a single instruction.
OpenClaw users must enable exec permissions first; otherwise the agent cannot run shell commands.
The README claims all tools are open source and all APIs are free.
The README says local use needs no proxy, while a server deployment may need a proxy for about one US dollar per month.
Credentials are stored locally in ~/.agent-reach/config.yaml with owner-only permissions and are not uploaded.
For platforms using cookies or login sessions, the README warns of platform detection and account-ban risk and recommends a dedicated alternate account.
Each platform uses an ordered primary-plus-fallback backend list.
The doctor command probes channels, reports the active backend, and a single channel failure does not take down the whole health check.
OpenCLI as a desktop backend requires a desktop environment and Chrome; after npm installation, the user must still click once in the Chrome extension store, and servers skip it automatically.
Reddit has no zero-configuration path because the anonymous interface is blocked and the official API uses approval, so a logged-in state is required.
The README attributes backend selection to real-device tests and says choices are reviewed periodically.

scripts.en: Agent Reach is a Python project under the MIT license that aims to give AI agents a single command-line way to read and search across internet platforms. Its README describes it as a capability layer rather than just another tool: it chooses among access routes, installs them, checks their health, and routes each platform to a working backend, while the agent itself calls the upstream tools to do the actual reading. It is meant for people using command-line-capable agents such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, Cursor, or Windsurf, and the maintainer also offers custom agent work for businesses. Representative uses include reading web pages, extracting YouTube subtitles and searching videos, reading RSS, working with GitHub, and accessing platforms such as Twitter, X, Bilibili, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, Xiaohongshu, LinkedIn, Boss Zhipin, V2EX, Xueqiu, and Xiaoyuzhou podcasts. Configuration needs vary by platform. A default install can activate several zero-configuration channels, and the agent asks before setting up platforms that need a login. Installation and updates can be started by sending the agent a single instruction. OpenClaw users must first enable exec permissions, or the agent cannot run shell commands. The README says all tools are open source and all APIs are free, with no proxy needed locally; a server deployment may need a proxy for about one dollar a month. Credentials are stored locally in a configuration file with owner-only permissions and are not uploaded. For platforms that use cookies or login sessions, the README warns about possible platform detection and account bans and recommends a dedicated alternate account. The project uses ordered primary and fallback backends for each platform. Its doctor command probes the channels and reports which backend is active; a single channel failure does not take down the whole health check. OpenCLI, used as a desktop backend for some platforms, requires a desktop environment and Chrome; after npm installs it, the user still has to click once in the Chrome extension store, and servers skip it automatically. Reddit has no zero-configuration path because the anonymous interface has been blocked and the official API uses approval, so a logged-in state is required. The README attributes its selection choices to real-device tests and says they are reviewed periodically.

summary: Repository packet for Panniantong/Agent-Reach. The README and v1.5.0 release describe a Python/MIT command-line capability layer for AI agents, with per-platform primary and fallback backends, installation and doctor checks, zero-config and login-required channels, local credential storage, and cookie or account-ban caveats. The corrected draft attributes enterprise Agent customization and implementation cooperation to the maintainer, not the project.
